what: R129 air control and landing tiers (P1-FL07; docs/research/fun-tracks.md R14-R16), one set for every car and every jump (R15: no per-jump or per-vehicle overrides). A crest hop is still the ground's (the car levels itself, owner playtest 1: a held throttle must not tip it onto its nose over a crest); after controlAfterS in the air (and unless a hit of knockDvMps in one tick threw it there: being knocked into the air isn't a jump, and isn't judged as a landing either), DRIVE y pitches the car as the wheels' reaction would (br-bbki.24, owner playtest 2026-10-17: throttle drops the rear and raises the nose, brake rotates the nose down) and DRIVE x yaws it, as body rates the car reaches within responseS whatever its inertia (br-bbki.26, owner 2026-10-31: 'the turning in the air is a little bit too aggressive': 50 deg/s yaw at full stick, down from 90, so a car in the air turns noticeably less; pitch stays 100 deg/s, so the stick still decides a clean, bad or crashed landing). With latchHeldInput, a steer a player was already holding at takeoff doesn't yaw the car until it has moved latchReleaseStick from it; a throttle pinned through the lip starts raising the nose after throttleLatchS in the air (a crest hop at full throttle tips nothing; a long jump over-rotates); roll is held level. A neutral stick holds the attitude, so the jump's lip pitch against its landing slope decides where neutral lands (R14). Landing after at least minAirS in the air is judged on the angle between the car's up and the ground's normal at first contact: clean (within cleanDeg, every attached wheel down within allWheelsS) boosts, OK costs nothing, bad (badDeg to crashDeg) loses speed, crash (past crashDeg, roof or side first) self-rights within crash.rightWithinS. Every number is a starting value tunable in ?tune; crates/jj-sim validates this file at load.
